cards.text: Absalom, King David's son, has been winning over the people of Israel, and his following keeps growing. Now a messenger comes to David with the news: “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”

cards.question: Israel's hearts are going to Absalom. What does David tell his servants in Jerusalem?

answers.text: Get up and flee before Absalom comes
Lock the gates and hold the city
Gather the army and march on Hebron

cards.text: David says they have to leave quickly, or Absalom will overtake them, heap disaster on them and put the city to the sword. The KING of Israel is getting out of his own city, friend, and he's getting out FAST.

cards.question: True or false: David's servants argue with him and beg him to stay and fight.

cards.text: His servants tell him that whatever the king decides, they're his servants. So David sets out, and his entire household follows him.

cards.question: David's household is leaving Jerusalem with him. Who does he leave behind to take care of the palace?

cards.text: The king stops at the last house, and all his servants march past him. There go the Cherethites and Pelethites, plus six hundred Gittites who followed him from Gath.

Then David turns to Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner and an exile, and tells him to go back and stay with the new king. Ittai only arrived yesterday, and David says he doesn't even know where he's going himself.

cards.question: David gives Ittai the Gittite a way out. What does Ittai say?

answers.text: Wherever the king goes he will be there
He will go back and serve the new king
He will head home and wait for news

cards.text: Life or death, Ittai is sticking with the king, and he's known him since YESTERDAY. I've had sprinkles stuck on my apron longer than that, so David says, “March on then.”

cards.question: True or false: Ittai marches on alone and sends all his men back.
David's people are passing through the countryside on their way out. What does the countryside do?

cards.text: Across the Kidron Valley they go, toward the wilderness. Then Zadok the priest arrives with Levites carrying the ark of God, and they set it down while Abiathar the priest offers sacrifices until everyone is out of the city.

cards.question: Zadok has the ark of God right there on the road out of the city. What does David tell him to do with it?

answers.text: Take it back to the city
Hide it in the Kidron Valley

cards.question: David is sending the ark of God back to Jerusalem. What does he say about it?

answers.text: If the LORD favors him He will bring him back
The road ahead is far too dangerous for it
The people in the city will need it to worship

cards.text: And if the LORD should say He doesn't delight in him? David says, “here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
David tells Zadok to go back to the city in peace with his son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan. Meanwhile, David will wait at the fords of the wilderness.

cards.question: David will wait at the fords of the wilderness. What is he waiting for?

answers.text: Word from Zadok in the city

cards.question: True or false: Zadok and Abiathar take the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stay there.

cards.text: David keeps going up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he goes. His head is covered, and he's walking barefoot.

cards.question: True or false: The people climbing the Mount of Olives with David cover their heads and weep too.

cards.text: Then someone tells David that Ahithophel, his own counselor, is among the conspirators with Absalom. That's like finding out the guy who runs your group chat started a brand new one, and you're not in it.

cards.question: Ahithophel has joined Absalom's side. What does David ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Bring Ahithophel back to David's side
Let Ahithophel fall in the next battle

cards.text: At the summit, where David used to worship God, his friend Hushai the Archite is there to meet him. Robe torn, dust on his head, and I bet he's ready to follow David anywhere.

cards.question: Hushai has come to meet David on the mountain. If Hushai goes on with him, what does David say he'll be?

cards.text: But David has a different job for Hushai. Go back to the city and tell Absalom he'll be his servant now, the way he used to serve his father.

cards.question: David wants Hushai back in Jerusalem, acting as Absalom's servant. What's the point?

answers.text: To talk Absalom into giving up

cards.question: David reminds Hushai that Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be in the city too. What should Hushai do with them?

answers.text: Report everything he hears from the palace
Help them keep the ark of God hidden
Stay out of sight in their homes

cards.question: Hushai will pass his news to the priests in Jerusalem. Who carries it out to David?

cards.text: Friend, this man is BAREFOOT on a mountain and still running the most organized operation I've ever seen. Off goes Hushai, back to Jerusalem.

cards.question: True or false: Hushai reaches Jerusalem just as Absalom is entering the city.

cards.text: And that's right where we'll stop for now. Trust me, friend, nobody in this story is done yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "March on then.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from before the passage: Absalom winning over the people (2 Samuel 15:6) and his following growing (2 Samuel 15:12). The card cites only 2 Samuel 15:13, so these facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "He's known him since YESTERDAY" stretches the text. David says Ittai "arrived only yesterday" (15:20), and 15:18 says the Gittites "had followed him from Gath." The text never says Ittai first met David yesterday.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "I've had sprinkles stuck on my apron longer than that, so David says, 'March on then'" uses "so" to tie Papa Dorin's joke to David's reply. That blends the comparison into the Bible scene and suggests a reason for David's words that the text doesn't give.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The card packs in more than two beats: crossing the Kidron toward the wilderness, Zadok and the Levites with the ark, setting the ark down, and Abiathar offering sacrifices until everyone has left. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "Zadok the priest arrives" adds an arrival. The text only says "Zadok was also there" (15:24).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Most story cards (5, 7, 8, 13, 16, 17) are plain retelling with no voice at all. The jokes on cards 3 and 10 are mild. Stop 1 reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend... If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "Ahithophel, his own counselor" comes from 2 Samuel 15:12, which is outside the passage. The card cites only 15:31, so the fact has no reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card calls Hushai "his friend", which comes from 15:37, but the card cites only 15:32.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The closing line is almost a copy of the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") instead of a new line written for this passage.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
